headline: Japan's Nikkei 225 fell about 1% in early trading on 9 October, led down by SoftBank, a big OpenAI investor, as doubts about AI and bond-market stress weighed on shares.
score_reason: Keeps the pool score: a clear knock-on from the OpenAI revenue story, but a modest index move.
importance_line: Japanese shares showed the same nervousness as Wall Street about AI companies' revenue, with SoftBank hit hardest because of its OpenAI stake; the move was small (about 1% on the index) and part of it was blamed on bond markets and oil.
summary: Reuters reports that Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1.06% in early trading on 9 Oct 2026, with SoftBank Group, a major investor in OpenAI, sinking 5.40% after the Financial Times reported that OpenAI's annualised revenue is $20 billion lower than earlier signalled. Sony Financial Group analysts told Reuters that the report set off a chain reaction of selling in related stocks, while stress in global bond markets and higher oil prices also weighed.
notes: Invezz page blocked by Cloudflare; Reuters report on the same trading day read on the Metrobank site (Reuters original link not available). Invezz reported SoftBank down about 6% and the Nikkei down 1%; Reuters early-trade figures used here.
